author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US is facing a series of recalls of fruit, vegetables and meat as an outbreak of food contaminations makes more people sick at a time when jobs focused on food safety have been cut. Michigan's largest lettuce producer, Revolution Farms, saw a decline in sales after the largest outbreak of cyclosporiasis linked to lettuce in Mexico hit the state, with more than 14,000 cases reported, nearly 400 hospitalisations and two deaths. Other foods recalled this summer include salmonella in jalapenos, eggs, mangoes and chicken, and E. coli in frozen berries and sprouts. While the number of food recalls is on par with previous years, health experts say contaminations and the level of risk are increasing. The Trump administration has faced scrutiny over hundreds of cuts to jobs focused on food safety, including labs that respond to cyclospora outbreaks. Farms are now seeing more interest in local sourcing and fresher ingredients as consumers seek reassurance. 

Al Jazeera's Matthew Torres repo
title: US food safety under scrutiny amid outbreaks and government job cuts

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Rescue teams in northern Nepal are continuing a difficult search for survivors at the Chilime hydropower plant, more than a week after devastating floods swept through the region. The Nepalese Army is flying helicopters in and out of a small landing strip every few minutes to bring in personnel and equipment, but the operation remains extremely dangerous because much of the riverbank and surrounding infrastructure was washed away. Rescue teams are also working to establish land access from both sides of the river so heavy equipment can be brought closer to the site. Despite the difficult terrain and poor weather, rescuers believe there could still be survivors inside the hydropower tunnels and are continuing efforts to reach them. The search comes after two workers were rescued alive from another hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa nine days after the floods, raising hopes for further survivors. 

Al Jazeera's Tony Cheng reports from northern Nepal.

Fourteen people remain missing, most of them young conscripts aged 18 or 19 who were serving their first year of national service. The blast destroyed a building at an artillery regiment, damaged nearby structures and injured more than 80 people. Officials say a stockpile of fireworks exploded, but the exact cause remains under investigation. Firefighters are continuing to search the debris for those still missing, while anxious families have gathered outside the site demanding information about their loved ones. Some relatives say missing soldiers were assigned to other duties and question why they were at the building when the explosion happened. Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz has promised a transparent investigation as authorities work to establish what caused the blast and whether proper safety protocols were followed.

On Saturday, the US military struck and destroyed three Iranian crude oil tankers near Kharg Island and in the Gulf of Oman, after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two US warships — an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Central Command says the US ships successfully evaded the attacks and no US personnel were harmed, while two of the Iranian vessels were disabled and the third completely destroyed. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said: "It's simple. If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy and sink their oil tankers." Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the US "acts of aggression", while the IRGC claimed it responded by targeting three oil tankers travelling through an "unauthorised" route in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels. There has been no independent confirmation of the Iranian claims. The tit-for-tat attacks mark a significant escalation between Washington and Tehran. 

Al Jazeera's Manuel Rapalo reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description: Fighting has intensified in western Yemen as government-aligned forces launch counterattacks against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, officially known as Ansar Allah, around Hodeidah and Taiz. Dozens of people, including civilians, were reported killed on Saturday as the Houthis pushed across several fronts before government forces sent reinforcements and launched their own air strikes. The fighting has also forced families to flee their homes around Maqbanah and Jabal Habashi, with some arriving at displacement camps with few belongings. Yemen has remained divided since the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014 and expanded their control across much of the north and west. A truce in 2022 reduced violence but failed to produce a lasting peace. The latest fighting is centred on a strategically important corridor leading towards the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a major global shipping route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A group of masked protesters dressed in black blocked traffic at the Port of Dover in the UK, chanting “Stop the boats” during an unannounced demonstration against illegal immigration.

The blockade disrupted operations at one of Britain’s busiest ports for several hours and caused significant traffic delays.

Local officials and residents criticised the protest, saying the demonstration was intimidating and did not represent the people of Dover.

The protest comes amid an ongoing political debate over immigration and small boat crossings in the English Channel. Despite the protesters’ demands, small boat arrivals have reportedly fallen by 44 percent this year.

Dover Council Leader Kevin Mills and local residents have condemned the demonstration, while the event has been described as part of the growing UK far-right “patriot movement”.

Police made no arrests and instead escorted the protesters to a train station.

Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec reports from Dover, UK.

title: Masked protesters blockade UK’s Port of Dover over immigration

More than 1,000 new suspected cases are being reported each day, according to the report, putting further pressure on an already overwhelmed healthcare system.

Parents describe the devastating impact of the disease, while health experts say malnutrition is contributing to the high death toll and making children more vulnerable to severe illness.

A mass vaccination campaign is now under way to contain the outbreak, but the highly contagious nature of measles continues to drive new infections.

Epidemiologists are calling for urgent and aggressive measures to bring the outbreak under control, described as the deadliest measles outbreak Bangladesh has experienced in decades.
